_about: SINGLE-TRANSLATION SHELF: one-off translations of history, travel, ideas, music and science from the first stretch of the single-translator list: Peter Martyr's De Orbe Novo (MacNutt, 1912), Morga's History of the Philippine Islands (Blair and Robertson), Pedro Sancho's Account of the Conquest of Peru (Means, 1917), Lobo's Voyage to Abyssinia (Samuel Johnson's translation, 1735), the Machiavelli of the Tudor Translations (Dacres's Discourses and Prince, 1636, with Whitehorne's Art of War), Dürer's journeys to Venice and the Low Countries, Hugo's History of a Crime, Lamartine's History of the Girondists, Gregorovius's Lucretia Borgia, Guizot's Memoirs, Blakman's Henry the Sixth (M. R. James, 1919), Nordenskiöld's Voyage of the Vega, Arago's Biographies of Distinguished Scientific Men, the Sand-Flaubert letters, Liszt's Chopin, Wagner's On Conducting, Tosi on florid song (Galliard, 1743), Feuillet's Orchesography (Weaver, 1706), Busoni's Sketch of a New Esthetic of Music, Saint-Saëns, Lilli Lehmann's How to Sing, Rolland's Musicians of To-day, Ardant du Picq's Battle Studies, Bernhardi, Boelcke and von Forstner, Froebel's autobiography, Preyer's Mind of the Child, Rosenkranz's Pedagogics, Hans Gross's Criminal Psychology, Fritz Müller's Facts and Arguments for Darwin, Ehrlich on the blood, Koch on tuberculosis, Basil Valentine, two seventeenth- and eighteenth-century treatises on chocolate, Holbach's Superstition in All Ages, Hertzka's Freeland, Wagner's The Simple Life, Tolstoy on Shakespeare, Faguet, Le Roy, Rathenau, Edward Lasker's Chess Strategy, fencing, and Hindu law. Each title gates on its own translator (_surname_by_slug). US public domain. Added 2026-10-10 by lane C (round 49); Adam may veto. No uids minted.
